name: two-lanes-four-passes-k14-of-21-scatter-zeros
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-width case, whose K = 0 and srcWidth = 0 skip every read and write. Here MPSTopKParameters (binding 29) holds K = 14, srcWidth = 21; kMPSUserConstant = 0 gives all four passes (kKU4O4 = 0), and kMPSNDArrayFunctionConstant = 0 clears accumulationOption, so writes go to postfixPrimary_f. 2 threads along x in one threadgroup. The first pass reads the row through prefixPrimary_4xf (retained module returns zeroinitializer) for columns 0 to 15 and prefixPrimary_f (retained writer returns 1.0) for columns 16 to 20, and zero-fills as it reads: the 4-wide part through the no-op postfixPrimary_4xf, the tail through postfixPrimary_f with 0.0. The selection is the forward kernel's (strict ogt to enter, strict olt to reorder, the partner's entry wins merge ties, later passes exclude earlier indices), so thread 0 selects columns [17, 19, 16, 18, 20, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15, 0] and scatters the gradient read through prefixSecondary_f (retained module returns 0.0) to each. Every write stores +0.0, so the observed words are +0.0 on the tail and the selected columns and the 0xab fill elsewhere, which pins the AIR's own deterministic tie rule (barrier-separated exchanges with fixed partners, no atomics); writes that meet on a column store the same +0.0, so order does not matter. Two lanes keep the multi-pass broadcast race-free. srcWidth bounds the read loops, log2 of the lane count the merge rounds, 4 the insertion and scatter loops.

name: concatenate-two-half4-tensors-along-x-through-one-merged-pointer
rationale:
A two-input tensor concatenation along x. A thread whose x is below the first tensor's width addresses src0 and one above it addresses src1, and the two addresses meet in a `phi ptr addrspace(1)` whose arms root in DIFFERENT descriptor bindings. That merge is the whole point: Logical SPIR-V has no pointer value that can be either buffer, so `native/psb_value_select.rs` rewrites it into the value domain -- load both candidates and select the loaded values. Measured with covgain.sh against every cased corpus source plus every public fixture, this 158-line module reaches 8 coverage rows nothing cased reaches, all in that file, including `apply_value_domain_rewrite`, `rewrite_cross_binding_pointer_merges_to_values::vreplay` and `rewrite_scalar_ptr_byte_loads`.

The dispatch is 8x3x3 against bounds of 6, 2 and 2, so 48 of the 72 threads take one of the three early returns and 24 do the copy. Of those, 16 read src0 (x < 4) and 8 read src1, so a merge that collapses to either arm is caught at 8 or 16 of the 24 destination slots: src0 carries values 1..115 and 400.. and src1 carries 200.. and 300.., which share no lane.

Every stride is a distinct parameter member -- src0's row stride is the split width itself, src1's is a separate member, and the two slice strides and the destination's row and slice strides are three more -- and all five differ (4, 2, 8, 4, 8, 16), so reading the wrong member of the 17-integer parameter block moves the read or the write. The destination x offset is 1, which puts the written block off the buffer origin: slots 0, 7, 8, 15, 16, 23, 24 and 31 are never written and must keep their fill, and every one of the 128 destination halves starts at a distinct value above 1000 that no source can produce.

The relu flag is on, so each loaded half4 passes through `air.fmax.v4f16` against zero. Lane 1 of every source element is the negation of lane 0, so the relu is observable at every one of the 24 writes -- lane 1 must read +0 and lanes 0, 2 and 3 must survive unchanged. A dropped relu leaves a negative half in lane 1 at all 24.

name: recover-bicubic-weights-from-one-hot-impulse-texels
rationale: Recovers the weights of Metal's bicubic filter (constexpr sampler filter::bicubic, address::clamp_to_edge, coord::normalized), which must be known before deciding whether VK_EXT_filter_cubic (Catmull-Rom) or any shader emulation reproduces Metal exactly. Each of the three 16x16 rgba32_float textures is made of single-texel impulses, so a filtered sample returns weights, not a colour blend: texture 0 (h) has texel (x, y) = the unit vector e(x mod 4), so channel c of a sample is the weight of the one horizontal tap whose column is congruent to c mod 4 (a four-tap footprint covers each residue exactly once) times the sum of the vertical weights; texture 1 (v) is e(y mod 4), the vertical weights times the horizontal sum; texture 2 (p) is e(x mod 4) on rows with y mod 4 == 0 and zero elsewhere, so channel c is one horizontal weight times the weight of the one vertical tap on such a row, which checks the 2D kernel's separability. Lane i reads its normalized coordinate (u, v) = ((bx + 0.5 + fx) / 16, (by + 0.5 + fy) / 16) from buffer 0 as binary32 (exact for every dyadic fraction below; for the two non-dyadic ones the sampled fraction is that of the rounded coordinate, 209715/2^21 for 0.1 and 699051/2^21 for 1/3) and writes the h, v and p samples at explicit level 0 (magnification) to out[3i], out[3i+1], out[3i+2] of buffer 1. Lanes 0-15 take fx = k/16 (k = 0..15), fy = 0, bx = 4 + k mod 4, by = 8, so the footprint's residues rotate through all four channel assignments; lanes 16-31 are the same vertically (fx = 0, fy = k/16, bx = 8, by = 4 + k mod 4); lanes 32-47 take fx = (2k+1)/32, fy = (31-2k)/32, bx = 4 + k mod 4, by = 4 + k div 4 (both axes fractional, every vertical residue on the zero row of p); lanes 48-59 take fine horizontal fractions 1/4096, 1/1024, 1/512, 1/256, 3/512, 1/128, 127/256, 129/256, 255/256, 4095/4096, 0.1f and 1/3f (fy = 0), which expose any quantization of the sub-texel fraction; lanes 60-63 are half-texel samples whose footprint crosses the left, right, top and bottom edge (bx = 0, bx = 15, by = 0, by = 15), so a clamped tap's weight lands in the edge texel's channel. With the taps at floor(u*16 - 0.5) - 1 .. + 2, lane i's channels in h are the four horizontal weights up to the known rotation, and the v sample of an fy = 0 lane holds the horizontal weight sum in channel by mod 4 (exactly 1 only if the weights are normalized). The weights tell the candidate filters apart: a nearest filter would return a single 1.0 per sample, a linear filter two weights 1 - f and f and no negative channel, Catmull-Rom (-f^3 + 2f^2 - f, 3f^3 - 5f^2 + 2, -3f^3 + 4f^2 + f, f^3 - f^2) / 2 gives (-1/16, 9/16, 9/16, -1/16) at f = 1/2, and a cubic B-spline (1, 23, 23, 1)/48 there. At fraction 0 in both axes the observed wrap-a-bicubic-sample-three-times-round case already returned the single texel, so lanes 0 and 16 (fx = fy = 0) should hold one exact 1.0 per sample. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB so an unwritten slot is visible; each lane writes only its own three float4s; the AIR has no loop.

name: float-products-flushed-before-rounding
rationale: Whether Metal flushes a float product whose exact value lies below 2^-126 but rounds to 2^-126 (tininess before rounding), in its compile without fast math, in vector and scalar multiplies and in dot's fused chain. Thread t reads the float4 operands a = in[2t] and b = in[2t + 1] and writes three float4 rows: a * b as one vector multiply; the same four products as scalar multiplies of scalar loads; and dot(a, b), dot(a.xy, b.xy), dot(a.zw, b.zw) and dot(a.yzw, b.yzw). 256 lanes: 10 hand lanes (an exact product of 2^-126 (1 - 2^-24), exactly 2^-126, just above it, the representable 2^-126 - 2^-149, and a product just below 2^-126 from operands above and below 1, each with both signs), 230 random lanes whose significand product lies within two units of 2^47 or 2^48 with exponent sums placing it next to 2^-126, both signs, and 16 ordinary products. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: the-exposure-floor-is-what-fmax-returns
rationale:
The cyclic AIR is bounded by one authored input: uniform member 24 (the sample count, at byte 120) is -1, and the loop is entered only when that member is greater than zero, so the accumulation over the 1D luminance texture never executes a single iteration and the running sum enters the tail as the phi's zero initializer.
The observed word is the exposure the kernel stores back into autoexposure member 1, and it is exactly the floor constant air.fmax.f32 is called with. Both inputs to the blend are authored zero: the stored exposure starts at 0 and the sum is 0, so the difference the blend scales is 0 and the blended exposure is 0 whatever the two exponentials return -- the case does not depend on air.exp.f32 or air.fast_exp.f32 being accurate, only on their being finite, because their result is multiplied by an authored zero. So the value reaching fmax is zero (or, if an exponential is a ULP off, a value on the order of 1e-14), and fmax against 1e-5f returns 1e-5f in every case. That is the whole answer: a lowering that returns the other operand, that takes a minimum, or that drops the floor entirely stores zero instead, which is also the authored initial byte pattern, so the qualification's differ-from-initial rule catches it too.

name: clamping-instead-of-wrapping-in-eight-families
rationale:
Eight uncovered air.* families in one invocation: air.add_sat.u.v3i8, air.sub_sat.u.v3i8, air.abs_diff.{u.i32,u.v2i16,u.v4i16,s.v4i32}, air.rhadd.u.i16 and air.mad_sat.s.i32 -- 18 corpus sources between them. All nineteen words were derived by hand before the GPU was asked and all nineteen came back as derived. Every family here is one where the WRAPPING version of the same arithmetic is a plausible lowering, so every lane names the wrapped answer it rejects.

addsat(200, 100) on a uchar is 255, not 44: the sum clamps at the type's maximum instead of wrapping. subsat(10, 100) is 0, not 166. The third lane of each, 255+1 and 255-1, sits one step from the same boundary on the side that does not clamp, so a lowering that clamped unconditionally is caught too.

absdiff is where an unsigned subtraction is most tempting and most wrong. absdiff(5u, 10u) is 5, not 4294967291; at ushort width absdiff(0, 65535) is 65535, not the 1 that 0 - 65535 wraps to. The signed member is the sharpest: absdiff(INT_MAX, INT_MIN) is 4294967295, which does not fit in the signed type at all -- the difference overflows int32 to -1 and abs(-1) is 1, so a lowering that subtracted at the operand width answers 1 here instead. That the result type of a SIGNED absdiff is UNSIGNED is the reason the true answer is representable, and Metal's own front end enforces it: assigning it to an int4 does not compile.

rhadd(3, 4) is 4. The rounded half-add is (a + b + 1) >> 1 while the plain hadd is (a + b) >> 1, and 3 and 4 are the smallest pair that separates them -- hadd answers 3.

madsat(100000, 100000, 0) is 2147483647. The exact product is 10^10, which saturates to INT_MAX; a plain multiply-add wraps to 1410065408.

The twentieth word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

rationale: The first authored device evidence for air.write_texture_1d.u.v4i32, and the carrier for the two image shapes whose SPIR-V capability the Dim enumerant does not settle. Dim 1D is enabled by either Sampled1D or Image1D and the type's Sampled operand decides which; the rule read that operand for the storage arm and not for the sampled one, so a write-only texture1d claimed both and demanded a capability for an image the module does not contain. This texture's four lanes use different arithmetic from the 1D texture's, so a write that lands on the wrong destination is a mismatch on both cases at once.
